role: Sole UI/UX Designer & UX Researcher · School project · 2025
title: HealthBuddy — SingHealth app redesign
problem: Patients found the app helpful but cluttered: appointments, queue status and payments were buried across screens. A live public healthcare service, so features could be reorganised but not removed, and one home screen had to serve outpatients, elderly users and general Singaporeans.
finding: All three personas hit the same wall: appointments mattered to 100% of respondents and queue status to 64.3%, yet 35.7% could not find queue tracking.
outcome: My paper sketch gave payment its own section, and the home screen still read as unrelated blocks. Iteration 2 merged queue and payment into one row and pulled Medicine, Results and Dependants into view; iteration 3 added colour, scale and status feedback. Scan went from three taps to one, and touch targets grew for elderly users who said they misclick.
